label: Sunday 22 November 2026
compiled: Compiled 22 Nov 2026, about 19:00 Vienna time, from the day's published headlines.

legend.red: War, attacks, deadly accidents or a severe crisis in today's news
legend.yellow: Tension, protests, disputes or mixed news

top.t: Russian drone strike collapses part of an apartment block near Kyiv
top.d: Rescuers searched the rubble in Dymer, Kyiv region, with around 14 to 15 people reported missing.

top.t: Iran strikes Bahrain as tension around the Strait of Hormuz rises
top.d: Bahrain reported an Iranian attack that set a civilian industrial site on fire and hurt two people; tankers were reported hit near Hormuz.

top.t: COP31 climate talks end without a deal
top.d: The EU and others rejected the final draft in Antalya as too weak, mainly because it left out fossil fuels.

top.t: Mexico captures cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro' after a deadly shootout
top.d: The FBI most-wanted fugitive was arrested after a firefight in Guasave, Sinaloa, that left at least 11 dead.
A confectionery factory near Jakarta burned from Saturday; police removed 24 body bags from the site.
The European-Japanese probe entered orbit around Mercury after an eight-year journey.

804.d: A Russian drone strike brought down part of an apartment block in Dymer, Kyiv region, with around 14 to 15 people missing. A strike on Kryvyi Rih on Saturday killed two and wounded 60.

643.d: The war with Ukraine continues. A Russian cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad was still burning in the Gulf of Finland after being hit by drones; it is unclear who struck it.

364.d: Daily nationwide power cuts began because power stations are short of fuel, amid the conflict with the US. Trump said he wants a 'permanent' deal with Iran.

048.d: Bahrain reported fresh Iranian attacks; one set a civilian industrial site on fire and injured two people. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they hit US radar sites.

887.d: The Houthis reported an airstrike on the capital, Sanaa.

275.d: Arson attacks on West Bank villages, blamed on Israeli settlers, left vehicles torched; Israel says it is investigating.

360.d: A confectionery factory in Serang, about 50 km from Jakarta, caught fire on Saturday. Police removed 24 body bags from the site.

566.d: A boat carrying mourners to a funeral overturned, killing at least 24 people.

484.d: Cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, 'El Chapo Isidro', was captured after a shootout in Guasave, Sinaloa, that left at least 11 dead.

729.d: The war continues; families displaced in Darfur face a hard winter.

050.d: At least 30 homes of Awami League members were reported set on fire.

376.d: Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot invited Netanyahu's Likud to coalition talks and condemned the West Bank arson attacks.

682.d: Air defences intercepted a Houthi drone aimed at the Riyadh region. Riyadh condemned the Iranian attack on Bahrain.

512.d: Tankers were reported attacked near Oman and the Strait of Hormuz.

784.d: The UAE condemned the attacks on Bahrain; Etihad extended cancellations on two Saudi routes until 30 November.

422.d: The UN force UNIFIL began handing its duties to the Lebanese army ahead of the end of its mandate.

706.d: The president's break with the UAE, a former ally, is tied to a power struggle with regional leaders.

792.d: COP31 in Antalya ended without a deal after the EU and others rejected the final draft put forward by Turkey and Australia.

036.d: COP31, co-led by Australia, collapsed; negotiations chief Chris Bowen called it very disappointing. The defence minister denied a US report about the AUKUS submarines.

620.d: Workers marched through Lisbon in heavy rain against the government's proposed budget and the cost of living.

250.d: Protesters marched in Paris on Saturday for higher public-sector pay and action on living costs.

724.d: Thousands took to the streets, alongside marches in Portugal and France.

826.d: The Suffolk village of Barnham held a symbolic vote to 'leave the UK' in protest at plans to house about 930 asylum seekers at a former RAF base.

276.d: The far-right AfD called for deporting 2.6 million Ukrainians, Syrians and Afghans.

246.d: A Russian cargo ship was still on fire off Finland, in the Gulf of Finland, after a drone attack.

840.d: The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal information database. Trump said he intends to reach a 'permanent' deal with Iran.

124.d: A reported Pentagon memo restricts some military co-operation with Canada; the defence minister said he had not seen it and that the forces still work closely.

076.d: Former president Jair Bolsonaro is in intensive care with a bowel obstruction and is reported stable.

710.d: Coalition talks continue after the local elections, with the ANC fighting to hold key councils. A wildfire in the Overberg was contained.

404.d: A proposed internet metering bill is raising privacy and affordability concerns.

764.d: PM Anutin Charnvirakul said the government will consider Gen Z protesters' demands if demonstrations stay lawful.

116.d: PM Hun Manet said the border closures with Thailand have not hurt Cambodia's production or farming.

458.d: Floods: the number of evacuees rose to 1,884 in Selangor and fell to 467 in Perak.

156.d: Beijing criticised a US ban on Chinese telecom firms' access to American phone numbers.

392.d: An autonomous air taxi completed a passenger flight without a pilot, and around 200 mascots paraded at a festival in Saitama.

356.d: Nepal's PM arrived in Delhi for talks with PM Modi, and Indian and Chinese commanders concluded another round of border talks.

524.d: PM Balendra Shah arrived in Delhi on his first bilateral visit to India.

704.d: Vietnam and China launched their 40th joint naval patrol in the Gulf of Tonkin.

760.d: Authorities destroyed 400 million captagon pills in a major drug haul.

068.d: Bolivia protected almost 715,000 acres of Amazon habitat, reported in this week's good-news roundup.

032.d: Boca Juniors won the Copa Sudamericana 2-0 on Saturday in Barranquilla.
